I had always believed that the Centre was something comical. I'm not laughibg now. This went from "shit the nail on the head" to crying for the sharks in one article.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I was forced to grip the toenail clippers with my teeth. I also ran out of baste.

I….uh…wow.

This is something really special right here. Easily the most ridiculous thing I’ve ever read, but just so good. Who would’ve guess Super ‘Roid-Rage was the thing that did the Centre in? Impeccable. Beautiful.

Sharks? Where we’re going, we don’t need sharks!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This is the best SPC content since '10:30 AM', I keep coming back to read the ending and can't stop smiling. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
For some reason this has given me the headcanon that all SPC people religiously follow the One Punch Man workout regimen.

There are no downsides to this.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I understand that this is a joke. Yet, I can’t help but feel this has enough good writing to ride the line and pass into canon territory. There were some legitimate feels in here. It took the absurd and played with your suspension of disbelief, poking and prodding to see how ridiculous it could get without losing your genuine emotional investment. At least, that’s what it did for me. Hearty +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Would be cool if they grew chest hair in the shape of a muscular arm

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Why else would Tsega drag themself to the cafeteria when their legs were fine?

I like to think that Tsega now scoots around the remains of Site-71 by skillfully undulating their torso and pulling themself forward with their tongue.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Though judging by the chat timestamps, this narrator is inhumanly good at tongue-typing.

Dr. Tsega was very popular at the unsanctioned orgies.

I’ve tried it

*Standing ovation*

…It also strikes me that it may have been quicker and easier for them to just punch their own arms off.

With that level of unbridled pugnative power, punching one's arm off would likely take out half the ribcage as well.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Okay, but this is canon now.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
All the sharks went to the one place no one would ever look. But, I mean — can you blame us? When you have guns like these, who has time to notice something so trifling as everyone's shoes simultaneously ceasing to fit?

Maybe we should have gotten a little suspicious when every kick-boxing match ended in a fatal shark-attack, though.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Clearly, the answer here is that they cannot conceive of using one's lower limbs as anything other than secondary combat appendages.

Did you notice how I never mentioned the characters were walking on their feet? This is actually a subtle implication that everyone is constantly doing handstands.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don’t know what I’ve just read, but my best guess is “continuing proof that this website has entered an age of artistic absurdism”. I can get into it.

Though judging by the chat timestamps, this narrator is inhumanly good at tongue-typing. I’ve tried it and I doubt I could get up to five words per minute.

…It also strikes me that it may have been quicker and easier for them to just punch their own arms off.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Sadly, I must ruin this by pointing out that he kicked the guy who originally suggested that the sharks weren’t coming back.

It could be that he lost the concept of using his feet after everything went to hell, though.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Along those lines, all I could think while reading this was that, living in a world that's so fist-oriented, the guy's using his tongue because he never considered the utility of feet. For like, anything. Even by the end, he hasn't considered using anything below the knee. It's amazing.

item.title: (no title)

item.title: (no title)

This is an expertly crafted piece of comedy, but I was surprised by how creeped out I was by Doctor Tsega's situation. Trapped in an abandoned complex, rabid punchers hammering at the walls…

+1 for surprise creepiness and "How are these servers even still up? Isn't that just the craziest thing…"

These arms were made for punching, and that's just what they did.

You have no idea how long I've waited for one of these.

I was not disappointed.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Man, i just

I don't

God, why?

I mean, my first thought was "Isn't SPC-001 supposed to be the ur-shark they're punching everything to keep at bay?" But then it turns into this amazingly ridiculous parody of end-of-the-world articles. Like, I never quite knew how to take it, it just gets more and more stupid and over the top as it goes and…

Nascency Impetus

???

What the hell?

EDIT: Upvoted for self-pugilism.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is the doomsday I never knew I needed. The possibility that they could still come back, just to finish off an army that was at its peak and ready for war is pretty depressing and scary.

Also, my favorite line:

"We punch underwater so you can live on the land."

item.title: It's The Best Kind Of Stupid
item.content:encoded:
My grandfather is an anesthesiologist. I should ask him about how many times he's had to use a green apple daiquiri to put a patient to sleep. The answer is zero but I just want to see the look on his face.

We've reached optimal doomsday everyone.
